title: MCP Integration
description: The boot service ships with an MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Other agents can generate memory shells and echo/probe shells directly through it.
endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.hint: The endpoint follows the current deployment address and keeps any reverse-proxy path prefix; Jar and Docker deployments default to http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp.
tools.title: Tools
tools.capabilities.description: Lists every supported server, shell tool, shell type, packer, probe method, obfuscation option and obfuscation scope.
tools.memshell.description: Generates a memory shell (Godzilla, Behinder, AntSword, Suo5, Command, etc.); same arguments as POST /api/memshell/generate.
tools.probe.description: Generates an echo/probe shell (DNSLog, ResponseBody, ResponseHeader, Sleep); same arguments as POST /api/probe/generate.
clients.title: Connect a client
clients.description: Examples for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Claude Desktop; any other Streamable HTTP client works with the same endpoint.
clients.desktopHint: Claude Desktop only supports stdio, so bridge it through mcp-remote (requires Node.js).
clients.restartHint: Restart the client after saving the configuration.
workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.step1: Call memshell_capabilities first to discover valid server, shellTool, shellType and packer values.
workflow.step2: Call generate_memshell or generate_probe_shell; the response contains class names, Base64 class bytes and the packed payload.
workflow.step3: Inject the payload into the target, then verify it with the matching client or a probe shell.
workflow.examplePrompt: Call memshell_capabilities first for valid parameters, then generate a Tomcat + Godzilla Filter memory shell.
security: For authorized security testing and research only.
